children: shares rose about 7% on Tuesday after its QNX unit
Coretura had selected its software for commercial vehicles.

Coretura was founded by Daimler Truck and Volvo Group to develop software for commercial vehicles. Coretura will use Alloy Kore, developed by QNX and Vector, as the software foundation for its vehicle platform.
The companies said the deal is the first customer win for Alloy Kore.

The platform combines QNX's operating system with software used for vehicle communications and other functions. Coretura is developing a common software platform for commercial vehicles that can be updated and improved after vehicles are sold.

BlackBerry, once known for its smartphones, has shifted its focus to software, with QNX at the center of its business. QNX software is used in more than 275M vehicles and is also used in areas including industrial automation, robotics, and medical devices.
on Thursday. In June, the company reported better-than-expected first-quarter results and raised its full-year outlook, citing growth in its QNX.
